title: Staff Product Analyst, Marketplace
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Delivery companies have always bought capacity by guesswork. Book too few drivers and parcels wait; book too many and you pay for empty vans. Most carriers accept that waste as the price of being reliable. Relay is building a marketplace where it isn't. You can't schedule drivers. You can only design what's on offer, and measure what happens.

Every part of our network runs on decisions. The next two years are about building the systems that make them well, and proving they do. Engineering and operational research build what you design.

MARKETPLACE HIGHLIGHTS

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what Marketplace changes on booking, matching and shifts, and recommend on pay. Our scientists' models and experiments feed your calls, and the squad lead acts on them.

- Drivers choose when to work. What makes a shift worth booking early, and how do you prove what works when a clean experiment isn't possible?

- Every booked shift is paid, used or not, and every unserved route means late parcels. Where should each area sit between the two, and what would let the network get there on its own?

- Local shops hold our parcels while running their own businesses. Where does the network need more of them, what should a shop be paid, and how would you see a closed shop coming?

- A whole area, not a slice: no playbook, and the result is on the street the next morning.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

THE OPPORTUNITY

As a Staff Product Analyst, Marketplace at Relay, you'll:

- Decide which Marketplace problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

- Design how Marketplace decides: which signals count, and what good looks like for booking, matching and pay.

- Tell the squad lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

- Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

- Go and look when the data and the street disagree: the sort centre, the van, the shop.

- Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, Marketplace's booking and pay decisions run on a system you designed.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR CANDIDATES WHO…

- Have owned the decisions a matching, pricing or incentive model fed, in a two-sided marketplace or gig platform, rather than building the model itself.

- Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or engineers built what you asked for.

- Can trace why drivers or couriers stop booking

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Supply Chain Operations sits within Anduril's central Supply Chain organization. It owns how material actually arrives, and the data and systems behind it: what suppliers ship, how it is packaged, labeled, and documented; the EDI and Supplier Portal connections that carry purchase orders, shipments, and invoices; and whether all of it can be received, processed, and put to use without touching a person twice. We make the operational requirements executable at every dock and every connection, across a rapidly growing and diverse supplier network. The work is measured in problems permanently removed, not tickets closed.

ABOUT THE JOB

You own the day-to-day health of EDI and the Supplier Portal. When a transaction fails, a trading partner cannot onboard, or an order, shipment, or invoice does not go through, you are responsible for resolving it. You implement and support the processes behind both systems, train suppliers on them, and analyze transaction data to identify what is breaking and why. You own the operational mechanics that make EDI and the Supplier Portal work, partnering with IT and Business Systems when a fix requires a system change.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Build and maintain data maps across supplier-facing systems, ERP and downstream reporting, defining field-level mappings, validation rules and supporting documentation that enable integrations and system implementations

• Support system implementation and enhancement projects alongside IT and Business Systems teams: gathering and documenting requirements, writing and executing test cases, validating data, and supporting training and rollout to internal teams and suppliers

• Create and maintain standard operating procedures, process maps and job aids for EDI and Supplier Portal processes, identifying automation and efficiency opportunities as transaction volume grows

Learn to Evaluate Freight, Not Just Find It
We are hiring Entry-Level Freight Dispatchers to support U.S. transportation operations with a focus on freight evaluation, load selection, mileage calculations, and operational planning.
This position is entry-level specifically in professional freight dispatching . Previous employment as a freight dispatcher is not required . Applicants must, however, have relevant exposure to U.S. trucking or transportation operations and a working understanding of freight load boards.
The right candidate should understand that a load cannot be evaluated by rate alone. Deadhead, loaded miles, equipment, appointments, driver availability, Hours of Service, and operating requirements all affect whether freight makes sense for a truck.
What You'll Evaluate

• Search DAT One, Truckstop, or comparable freight load boards.

• Compare available freight by lane, equipment type, mileage, rate, and appointment requirements.

• Calculate loaded miles, deadhead miles, total trip miles, and rate per mile.

• Identify excessive deadhead and inefficient freight options.

• Review pickup and delivery schedules for operational feasibility.

• Consider available driver Hours of Service when evaluating loads.

• Determine whether available equipment is appropriate for the freight.

• Identify potential delays, accessorial considerations, and unusual load requirements.

• Organize suitable freight options for authorized review and booking.

Understanding Freight Economics
Freight evaluation requires looking beyond the advertised load rate.
You will be expected to understand how factors such as:

• Loaded mileage

• Deadhead mileage

• Rate per mile

• Equipment type

• Pickup and delivery appointments

• Driver Hours of Service

• Freight lanes

• Driver location and availability

• Potential detention or other accessorial situations

affect the operational value of a load.
Applicants should be comfortable working with mileage calculations, spreadsheets, freight information, and basic trip economics.
Relevant Transportation Background
Prior professional freight-dispatch employment is not required .
Relevant experience or knowledge may come from:

• CDL-A truck driving

• Owner-operator or fleet operations

• Transportation coordination

• Truck-driver recruiting with practical trucking knowledge

• Freight brokerage support

• Carrier operations

• Load planning

• Logistics or transportation operations

Applicants must have enough U.S. trucking knowledge to understand basic freight terminology, equipment, mileage, lanes, and load-board information.

• Working understanding of driver Hours-of-Service considerations.

• Ability to communicate professionally with drivers, brokers, carriers, and transportation personnel.

• Strong attention to detail and accurate recordkeeping.

• Computer proficiency and reliable internet access.

• Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Additional Responsibilities
